classification.difficultyReason: Choose triangle ADC, find an intermediate angle using inverse sine, reject its supplement because the triangle is already obtuse, then calculate the remaining angle and apply the sine rule again.

content.prompt: $ABCD$ is a parallelogram. $\angle CDA=130^\circ$, the long diagonal $AC$ is $50\text{ m}$ and $AD=30\text{ m}$. Find the length of the side $DC$, correct to one decimal place.

spec.description: Parallelogram ABCD with diagonal AC, length labels and the 130-degree interior angle at D. Opposite sloping sides have single parallel arrows; opposite horizontal sides have double parallel arrows. Decorative blue strokes are rendered in house black.
spec.mathematics: AC=50 m, AD=30 m, angle CDA=130 degrees. AB is parallel to DC and BC is parallel to AD.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source-supplied givens are visible; DC remains unlabelled.

answer.short:
$DC\approx25.1\text{ m}$.

Use the sine rule twice in $\triangle ADC$, finding an intermediate angle first.
answer.worked:
In $\triangle ADC$, the sine rule gives
$$\begin{align*}\sin\angle ACD&=\frac{30\sin130^\circ}{50}\\\angle ACD&=\sin^{-1}\!\left(\frac{30\sin130^\circ}{50}\right).\end{align*}$$
The angle is acute because the triangle already contains an obtuse angle. Using the unrounded value,
$$\begin{align*}\angle CAD&=180^\circ-130^\circ-\angle ACD\\\angle CAD&\approx22.63698044^\circ.\end{align*}$$
Apply the sine rule again, retaining the unrounded angle:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{DC}{\sin\angle CAD}&=\frac{50}{\sin130^\circ}\\DC&=\frac{50\sin\angle CAD}{\sin130^\circ}\\DC&\approx25.1\text{ m}.\end{align*}$$
